title: The Who take shape in London
description: With Roger Daltrey, Pete Townshend, John Entwistle and Keith Moon, the group became known for loud, aggressive power-chord rock and destructive stage shows.

title: Tony Iommi loses fingertips in a factory accident
description: On his last day at a Birmingham sheet-metal factory, Tony Iommi severed the tips of two fingers on his fretting hand. He made thimble-like prosthetics and used lighter strings, which shaped his heavy, down-tuned style.

title: Scorpions form in Hanover
description: Rudolf Schenker's band became West Germany's biggest metal export. Michael Schenker and Klaus Meine were part of its early history.

title: Cream forms in London
description: Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker formed one of rock's first supergroups. Their loud, improvised trio format set a template for heavy bands.

title: The Jimi Hendrix Experience forms in London
description: Hendrix moved from New York to London and put together a trio with Noel Redding and Mitch Mitchell. Within months they were hits in Britain.

title: The Stooges form in Ann Arbor
description: Iggy Pop, the Asheton brothers and Dave Alexander formed the band in Michigan. Their crude, confrontational sound pre-dated punk by years.

title: Blue Cheer forms in San Francisco
description: The trio built a reputation for playing at extreme volume. Their 1968 debut is cited as an early heavy-metal record.

title: Hendrix sets his guitar on fire at Monterey Pop
description: The Experience's set at the Monterey International Pop Festival introduced Hendrix to American audiences. It ended with him setting his guitar alight.

title: Black Sabbath begin as Earth in Birmingham
description: Tony Iommi, Ozzy Osbourne, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward started out playing blues-rock as Earth. They renamed themselves Black Sabbath in 1969 and began writing darker, heavier material.

title: Deep Purple forms
description: Formed in Hertford originally as Roundabout, they later became one of the leading hard rock acts of the early 70s. Their 1970 album In Rock moved decisively to heavier material.

title: Led Zeppelin forms
description: Jimmy Page assembled Robert Plant, John Paul Jones and John Bonham to fulfil Yardbirds commitments, first as the New Yardbirds. The new name followed within weeks.

title: Judas Priest forms in the West Midlands
description: The band began in 1969 around singer Al Atkins. Guitarist K.K. Downing and bassist Ian Hill joined in 1970, and Rob Halford in 1973.

title: Hawkwind forms in London
description: The psychedelic space-rock group later employed Lemmy Kilmister as bassist and singer, from 1971 to 1975.

title: Jimi Hendrix dies in London
description: Hendrix died at age 27 after asphyxiating on vomit following barbiturate use. His career had lasted barely four years.

title: The Van Halen brothers form Mammoth
description: In Pasadena, Eddie and Alex Van Halen began the band that would become Van Halen after David Lee Roth joined and took over vocals. The group built its reputation in Southern California clubs.

title: Bowie performs 'Starman' on Top of the Pops
description: The BBC broadcast made Ziggy Stardust a national phenomenon. The performance influenced many young British musicians.

title: Rob Halford joins Judas Priest
description: His wide vocal range and later his leather-and-studs image became defining features of metal. Priest's identity took shape from that point.

title: Kiss forms in New York City
description: Paul Stanley, Gene Simmons, Ace Frehley and Peter Criss adopted make-up and a pyrotechnic stage show. Their image shaped the look of 1980s metal.

title: AC/DC forms in Sydney
description: Brothers Malcolm and Angus Young formed the band in Australia's capital of live rock. Bon Scott joined as singer in 1974.

title: Bon Scott becomes AC/DC's singer
description: The ex-Fraternity singer's rough charisma and lyrics gave the band its voice. His tenure ended with his death in 1980.

title: Ramones form in Queens
description: Joey, Johnny, Dee Dee and Tommy Ramone adopted the shared stage surname and a stripped-down, fast style. Their approach is a pillar of punk and an inspiration for thrash.

title: Raven forms in the north-east of England
description: The Gallagher brothers' band played at breakneck pace and became one of NWOBHM's loudest acts. They toured the US with an unknown Metallica in 1983.

title: The Stooges break up
description: After a chaotic final period, the band ended in early 1974. They reformed decades later, by which time punk had made them legends.

title: California Jam at Ontario Motor Speedway
description: Deep Purple and Emerson, Lake & Palmer co-headlined the huge festival, which was broadcast on ABC television. Black Sabbath also played.

title: Ramones play CBGB for the first time
description: The band started a residency at the New York club that became the base of the American punk scene. Early gigs were short and very fast.

title: Saxon begin in Barnsley as Son of a Bitch
description: The band changed its name to Saxon in 1979 and became part of the NWOBHM.

title: Sex Pistols form in London
description: Managed by Malcolm McLaren, Johnny Rotten, Steve Jones, Paul Cook and Glen Matlock brought punk to Britain's mainstream.

title: Ritchie Blackmore leaves Deep Purple and forms Rainbow
description: Blackmore left in 1975 to start Rainbow with Ronnie James Dio. Their fantasy-themed, classically influenced metal later shaped power metal.

title: Lemmy is fired from Hawkwind
description: After an arrest at the Canadian border, the bassist was dismissed. He promptly set out to form his own band.

title: Lemmy forms Motörhead
description: Named after the last song he wrote for Hawkwind, the band mixed punk's speed with blues-rock volume. Lemmy declared they would play louder than anyone.

title: Steve Harris forms Iron Maiden
description: The bassist founded the band in Leyton, East London on Christmas Day 1975. Its early line-ups changed often before the 1979 breakthrough.

title: Diamond Head forms in Stourbridge
description: Their complex riffs and 1980 album Lightning to the Nations were studied by young Metallica members.

title: Black Flag forms in Hermosa Beach
description: Greg Ginn's band, first called Panic, became hardcore's most influential act. Its heavy, relentless sound reached metal fans.

title: Accept forms in Solingen
description: Udo Dirkschneider and Wolf Hoffmann's band developed a staccato, gang-vocal style that influenced thrash and power metal.

title: Ramones play London's Roundhouse
description: Their show in the UK capital inspired many in the British punk scene, including future members of the Clash and others.

title: Sex Pistols swear on Bill Grundy's TV show
description: Their expletives on live television created a media scandal. It made the band notorious overnight.

title: Misfits form in Lodi, New Jersey
description: Glenn Danzig and Jerry Only built a sound out of punk, doo-wop and B-movie horror. Their imagery later inspired many metal bands.

title: Discharge forms in Stoke-on-Trent
description: Their fast, repetitive d-beat drumming and relentless noise shaped hardcore, thrash and extreme metal.

title: Bad Brains forms in Washington, D.C.
description: They started as a jazz-fusion band and turned to extremely fast hardcore. Their speed influenced punk and thrash.

title: Def Leppard forms in Sheffield
description: The teenage band joined the NWOBHM before moving to a polished, radio-friendly sound with producer Mutt Lange.

title: Venom forms in Newcastle
description: Cronos, Mantas and Abaddon deliberately played louder, faster and more Satanic than anyone else. Their approach shaped black, thrash and death metal.

title: Dead Kennedys forms in San Francisco
description: Jello Biafra's band mixed surf-tinged hardcore with sharp political satire. The Bay Area hardcore scene grew around them.

title: Sex Pistols play their last show of the original line-up
description: After the final US tour date at San Francisco's Winterland, the band broke up. Their one studio album remained a landmark of punk.

title: Keith Moon dies
description: The Who's drummer died in London aged 32. His wild style and showmanship influenced rock and metal drummers.

title: The Exploited form in Edinburgh
description: Wattie Buchan's band took punk toward louder and faster territory. Their crossover with metal grew in the 1980s.

title: Exodus forms in Richmond, California
description: Kirk Hammett was a founding guitarist. The band became one of the cornerstones of the Bay Area thrash scene.

title: Neal Kay's Soundhouse becomes a NWOBHM hub
description: Kay ran the heavy metal disco in North London, where fans heard new bands over a huge sound system. Demo tapes played there helped get bands including Iron Maiden noticed.

title: Ronnie James Dio joins Black Sabbath
description: The former Rainbow singer brought a more melodic and fantasy-driven approach. Heaven and Hell followed in 1980.

title: Ozzy Osbourne starts a solo band
description: He recruited guitarist Randy Rhoads and began recording Blizzard of Ozz. Rhoads' classically informed playing set the course.

title: Ozzy Osbourne is dismissed from Black Sabbath
description: The band had been in difficulty through drugs and creative disagreements. The change of vocalist opened a new chapter for both parties.

title: Sounds writers coin 'New Wave of British Heavy Metal'
description: The British weekly Sounds, through writer Geoff Barton and editor Alan Lewis, gave a name to the scene of bands like Iron Maiden, Saxon and Venom. The label stuck.

title: Overkill forms in New Jersey
description: Bobby 'Blitz' Ellsworth and D.D. Verni's band later became one of the East Coast's leading thrash acts.

title: Roadrunner Records is founded in the Netherlands
description: The label began as an import business and became a major home of thrash and death metal, including Sepultura and Obituary.

title: Suicidal Tendencies forms in Venice, California
description: Mike Muir's group began as skate-punk and moved toward thrash. They became leaders of the crossover scene.

title: Metal for Muthas compilation released
description: EMI's compilation of NWOBHM bands included Iron Maiden and brought attention to the scene. It helped spread the new wave beyond London.

title: Bon Scott dies
description: AC/DC's singer died in London aged 33 after a night of heavy drinking. The band nearly stopped but continued.

title: Brian Johnson joins AC/DC
description: The former Geordie singer replaced Bon Scott. Back in Black followed in July 1980.

title: First Monsters of Rock at Castle Donington
description: Rainbow headlined, with Judas Priest, Scorpions, April Wine, Saxon, Riot and Touch. It became an annual British metal festival.

title: John Bonham dies
description: Led Zeppelin's drummer died after a day of heavy drinking. The inquest ruled it accidental death.

title: Led Zeppelin announce they are splitting
description: The band said they could not continue without Bonham. Their influence on metal remained enormous.

title: Lars Ulrich places an ad in The Recycler
description: The Danish-born drummer sought other musicians for a metal band. James Hetfield answered it.

title: Slayer forms in Huntington Park
description: Kerry King, Jeff Hanneman, Tom Araya and Dave Lombardo formed the band. It became the dark heart of the Big Four.

title: Anthrax forms in New York
description: Scott Ian and Danny Lilker started the band, which became the East Coast's thrash leader.

title: Mötley Crüe forms in Los Angeles
description: Nikki Sixx, Tommy Lee, Mick Mars and Vince Neil brought theatrical glam to the Sunset Strip metal scene.

title: Mercyful Fate forms in Copenhagen
description: King Diamond's group blended falsetto vocals, occult themes and intricate guitar work. Their influence on thrash and black metal was large.

title: Dark Angel forms in Los Angeles
description: The group became known for fast, complex thrash with Gene Hoglan on drums in the mid-80s.

title: Pantera forms in Arlington, Texas
description: Brothers Dimebag Darrell and Vinnie Paul started with glam metal. They later reinvented themselves as a groove-driven metal band.

title: Sodom forms in Gelsenkirchen
description: Tom Angelripper's trio drew on Venom and Motörhead. They became one of the German thrash trio.

title: Napalm Death forms in Birmingham
description: The band began as a punk-influenced group and changed its line-up often. By 1987 they were creating grindcore.

title: Kerrang! publishes its first issue
description: It began as a one-off special of Sounds, with Angus Young on the cover. It then became a permanent magazine covering heavy metal.

title: MTV launches
description: The music channel gave metal and hard rock a new platform. Video exposure became a key part of the business.

title: Bruce Dickinson joins Iron Maiden
description: The former Samson singer replaced Paul Di'Anno. His operatic voice defined the classic Maiden sound.

title: Metallica forms in Los Angeles
description: Lars Ulrich and James Hetfield started the band after Ulrich's ad. Their fast, aggressive style grew out of NWOBHM and punk.

title: Jon and Marsha Zazula found Megaforce Records
description: The New Jersey couple released early Metallica and later Anthrax. Their label helped launch thrash on the East Coast.

title: Tape trading builds the thrash underground
description: Fans mailed copies of demos worldwide, spreading bands like Metallica faster than record labels could. Fanzines supported the network.

title: Kreator forms in Essen as Tormentor
description: The German band formed alongside Sodom and Destruction as part of the German thrash scene.

title: Number of the Beast draws religious protests in the US
description: Some groups objected to Iron Maiden's album and its Satanic imagery. The controversy made the band better known.

title: Dio leaves Black Sabbath
description: He departed after disputes during the mixing of the live album Live Evil and formed his own band.

title: Cliff Burton joins Metallica
description: The Trauma bassist, with his classical-influenced style, joined on the condition that the band relocate to the Bay Area. The move came in early 1983.

title: Ronnie James Dio forms Dio
description: After leaving Black Sabbath, he started his own band with drummer Vinny Appice. Holy Diver came in 1983.

title: Hellhammer forms in Zürich
description: Tom G. Warrior and Martin Eric Ain's crude, primitive band was derided at the time. It later became a cult influence on black and death metal.

title: Destruction forms in Lörrach
description: Originally called Knight of Demon, they took their new name in 1983 and became a key German thrash act.

title: Death Angel forms in Daly City
description: Five Filipino-American cousins and friends started the band as teenagers. They rose from the Bay Area scene.

title: Voivod forms in Jonquière, Quebec
description: The Canadian band mixed punk and thrash with science-fiction imagery. Over time they became one of metal's most progressive acts.

title: Metallica play their first show
description: The band performed at Radio City in Anaheim, California. They were still without a stable line-up.

title: Randy Rhoads dies in a plane crash
description: Ozzy Osbourne's guitarist died in Leesburg, Florida aged 25. His classically influenced playing was a major influence on metal guitarists.

title: Metal Massacre compilation released
description: Brian Slagel's Metal Blade compilation featured Metallica's first recorded song, 'Hit the Lights', misspelled on the cover as 'Mettallica'. It started Metal Blade Records.

title: Metallica play San Francisco's Old Waldorf with Exodus
description: Exodus opened for Metallica at the club, a key meeting point of the Bay Area scene. The Bay Area scene was already forming around such shows.

title: Dave Mustaine forms Megadeth
description: After leaving Metallica, Mustaine started Megadeth with bassist David Ellefson. The band built a reputation for technical thrash.

title: Testament forms in Berkeley as Legacy
description: The band formed in the East Bay and became Testament in 1986, with Chuck Billy as singer.

title: Bathory forms in Stockholm
description: Quorthon's solo project drew on Venom's sound and became a forefather of black metal.

title: Possessed forms in the Bay Area
description: Jeff Becerra's group helped establish a blend of thrash and a darker, more guttural extreme sound.

title: Chuck Schuldiner forms Mantas, later Death
description: The Florida teenager built the band from a love of Venom and Slayer. They renamed it Death in 1984.

title: Morbid Angel forms in Tampa
description: Trey Azagthoth started the band in Florida. Their technical, dark death metal made them central to the Tampa scene.

title: Noise Records is founded in Berlin
description: Karl-Ulrich Walterbach's label released Kreator, Helloween, Celtic Frost and many other European metal bands.

title: Kirk Hammett joins Metallica
description: The Exodus guitarist replaced Mustaine for the recording of Kill 'Em All. He has remained with the band since.

title: Dave Mustaine is dismissed from Metallica
description: After clashes with Hetfield and Ulrich, the lead guitarist was sent home from New York. He soon started Megadeth.

title: Heavy Metal Day at the US Festival
description: The California festival's metal day featured Van Halen, Ozzy Osbourne, Judas Priest, Scorpions, Mötley Crüe and others. It put the genre before a huge American crowd.

title: Metallica and Raven tour as 'Kill 'Em All for One'
description: The two-month US club tour with the British band Raven, starting days after the album came out, was Metallica's first national tour.

title: Kiss appear without make-up on MTV
description: The band ended their make-up era on television, a calculated move to revive their career. It reflected how MTV could reshape image.

title: Quiet Riot's Metal Health reaches number one
description: The LA band's album was the first heavy metal record to top the Billboard 200. It showed major-label potential for the genre.

title: Sepultura forms in Belo Horizonte
description: Brothers Max and Igor Cavalera started the band in Brazil. They took their name from a Motörhead lyric.

title: Celtic Frost forms in Zürich
description: Tom G. Warrior and Martin Eric Ain evolved from Hellhammer. Their avant-garde extreme metal influenced death and black metal.

title: Joey Belladonna joins Anthrax
description: The singer's clean, powerful vocals defined their classic 80s sound.

title: Possessed record the 'Death Metal' demo
description: The demo helped popularise the term 'death metal' for the sound the band and others were developing.

title: The German thrash trio rises
description: Kreator, Sodom and Destruction built a distinctive, raw European thrash sound, helped by the label Noise.

title: Mayhem forms in Norway
description: The band, started by Euronymous and Necrobutcher, became one of the central acts of Norwegian black metal.

title: This Is Spinal Tap premieres in the US
description: Rob Reiner's mockumentary satirised heavy metal excess. Many real bands recognised themselves in it.

title: Deep Purple's classic line-up reunites
description: Ian Gillan, Ritchie Blackmore, Roger Glover, Jon Lord and Ian Paice reformed after a decade apart. Perfect Strangers followed that autumn.

title: Metallica sign to Elektra
description: Elektra signed the band after seeing them live and reissued Ride the Lightning that November. Master of Puppets was the first album they made for the label.

title: Hanoi Rocks drummer Razzle killed in a car crash
description: Vince Neil of Mötley Crüe was driving drunk. The accident made headlines and highlighted the dangers of excess in the scene.

title: Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen loses his left arm
description: Allen lost his arm in a car accident in Sheffield. He learned to play with a customised electronic kit and remained in the band.

title: S.O.D. forms in New York
description: Scott Ian, Charlie Benante, Dan Lilker and Billy Milano formed it as a joke band. It helped create crossover.

title: Ruthie's Inn becomes a Bay Area metal home
description: The Berkeley club hosted many thrash and death metal bands. Together with the Old Waldorf and The Stone it anchored the Bay Area scene.

title: Carcass forms in Liverpool
description: Bill Steer and Ken Owen founded the band, which started with grind and gore and evolved toward melodic death metal.

title: Earache Records is founded in Nottingham
description: Digby Pearson's label became the home of grindcore and death metal, releasing Napalm Death, Carcass and Morbid Angel.

title: Crossover thrash blends hardcore and metal
description: D.R.I., Suicidal Tendencies, S.O.D., Cro-Mags and others joined punk's speed to metal's heaviness. The scene brought both audiences to the same shows.

title: Mercyful Fate break up; King Diamond goes solo
description: King Diamond left to form a solo band under his own name. Fatal Portrait and Abigail followed.

title: First Rock in Rio opens
description: The Brazilian festival booked Iron Maiden, Ozzy Osbourne, AC/DC, Scorpions and Whitesnake among others. It showed the global scale of metal.

title: The Parents Music Resource Center is founded
description: The group, started by Tipper Gore and others in Washington, campaigned for warning labels on records. Metal became a prime target.

title: Black Sabbath reunite with Ozzy at Live Aid
description: The original line-up played at the charity concert in Philadelphia. It was a rare reunion of the four.

title: Metallica play Donington's Monsters of Rock
description: The Californian band appeared on a bill headlined by ZZ Top. It was an early British exposure to a large crowd.

title: PMRC hearing in the US Senate
description: Frank Zappa, Dee Snider and John Denver testified against music labelling. The hearing led to Parental Advisory stickers.

title: Slayer sign to Def Jam
description: Rick Rubin's hip-hop label took on the thrash band. The pairing produced Reign in Blood.

title: Steve 'Zetro' Souza replaces Paul Baloff in Exodus
description: The new vocalist took Exodus into their next phase, beginning with Pleasures of the Flesh.

title: First Dynamo Open Air in the Netherlands
description: The Eindhoven festival, held by the Dynamo club, grew into one of Europe's main metal festivals.

title: Phil Lynott dies
description: The Thin Lizzy singer and bassist died aged 36, after a period of illness following drug problems. His band's twin-guitar sound remained a model for metal.

title: Metallica tour with Ozzy Osbourne
description: The US arena run exposed Metallica to a larger audience after Master of Puppets.

title: Cliff Burton dies in Sweden
description: Metallica's bassist was killed when the tour bus skidded off the road near Ljungby. He was 24.

title: Jason Newsted joins Metallica
description: The Flotsam and Jetsam bassist replaced Burton. The band decided to continue.

title: Columbia refuses to distribute Reign in Blood
description: The label objected to the album's lyrics, and Geffen released it instead. The incident added to Slayer's notoriety.

title: Bay Area second wave of thrash
description: Death Angel, Testament, Vio-lence, Forbidden and Heathen followed Metallica and Exodus. The area was the world's busiest thrash scene.

title: Phil Anselmo joins Pantera
description: The New Orleans singer replaced Terry Glaze and the band shifted from glam to a heavier style. Cowboys from Hell followed in 1990.

title: Headbangers Ball premieres on MTV
description: The weekly metal video show gave bands without radio play a national platform.

title: Napalm Death record their first John Peel session
description: The BBC Radio 1 DJ played their ultra-fast songs and helped spread grindcore. Peel kept featuring extreme bands in later years.

title: Death record at Morrisound in Tampa
description: The studio's work with Scott Burns helped build a distinctive Florida death metal sound.

title: Sepultura sign to Roadrunner Records
description: The deal brought the Brazilian band to an international audience.

title: Two fans die at Donington's Monsters of Rock
description: The bill included Iron Maiden, Kiss, David Lee Roth and Guns N' Roses. Two fans were killed in a crowd crush.

title: Metallica release their first music video, for 'One'
description: The video helped bring the band to MTV audiences.

title: Jethro Tull beat Metallica at the Grammys
description: The first Best Hard Rock/Metal Performance award went to the flute-playing band, surprising the metal world. Metallica performed 'One' on the show.

title: Moscow Music Peace Festival
description: Bon Jovi, Mötley Crüe, Ozzy Osbourne, Scorpions, Skid Row and others played at Lenin Stadium. The shows signalled the reach of hard rock and metal behind the Iron Curtain.

title: Sunlight Studio shapes Swedish death metal
description: Entombed and other Stockholm bands recorded at Sunlight with producer Tomas Skogsberg. Their buzzsaw guitar tone became the scene's signature.

title: First Wacken Open Air
description: The German festival started small and grew into one of the world's largest heavy metal festivals.

title: Marty Friedman and Nick Menza join Megadeth
description: The new guitarist and drummer helped Mustaine's band reach a technical peak on Rust in Peace.

title: Judas Priest cleared in the 'subliminal message' trial
description: A Nevada judge dismissed the suit alleging hidden messages in a song had caused two fans' suicide attempts. The case drew attention to heavy metal's controversies.

title: Clash of the Titans tour begins
description: The tour paired Megadeth, Slayer, Testament and Suicidal Tendencies on a European run, then returned to the US the following year with Alice in Chains.

title: Death Angel's tour bus crashes
description: Drummer Andy Galeon was seriously injured and the band went on hiatus. They resumed years later.

title: Rock in Rio II
description: The second festival at the Maracanã stadium included Judas Priest among other acts.

title: Anthrax and Public Enemy collaborate on 'Bring tha Noize'
description: The rap and metal groups' joint version of a Public Enemy song and tour were early landmarks of rap metal.

title: Nirvana release Nevermind
description: The album's success shifted mainstream rock toward alternative bands. Many 80s metal acts fell from fashion.

title: Monsters of Rock in Moscow
description: AC/DC, Metallica, Pantera, The Black Crowes and E.S.T. played to a huge crowd at Tushino Airfield, a landmark of the Soviet Union's last months.

title: Rob Halford leaves Judas Priest
description: The singer departed to pursue other projects, leaving Priest without its voice. The group later hired Tim 'Ripper' Owens.

title: Dave Lombardo leaves Slayer
description: The drummer's departure after a dispute removed a key part of the sound. He later returned.

title: Anthrax part with Joey Belladonna
description: John Bush replaced him as the band shifted toward a heavier sound.

title: James Hetfield is burned by pyrotechnics in Montreal
description: On the joint stadium tour with Guns N' Roses, Hetfield walked into a pyrotechnic flame at Olympic Stadium and suffered serious burns. The tour resumed weeks later with Metal Church guitarist John Marshall filling in on rhythm guitar.

title: Ozzy Osbourne plays what he calls his farewell show
description: The Costa Mesa shows ended his No More Tears tour. The original Black Sabbath line-up joined him on stage for the final songs.

title: Bruce Dickinson leaves Iron Maiden
description: He announced his departure early in 1993 and played farewell shows that August. Blaze Bayley replaced him.

title: Pantera's Far Beyond Driven debuts at number one
description: The extreme, heavy album topped the US charts. It showed that hard metal could still sell in the grunge era.

title: Kurt Cobain dies
description: Nirvana's singer was found dead on April 8, with the death dated to April 5. His death marked the end of the grunge breakthrough.

title: Tim 'Ripper' Owens joins Judas Priest
description: The Priest tribute-band singer became the band's new vocalist after Halford's departure.

title: Ramones play their last show
description: The Los Angeles concert closed a 22-year career. The band's influence on thrash and punk lasted.

title: Max Cavalera leaves Sepultura
description: The founding singer and guitarist left after disputes. Derrick Green replaced him.
